subject.title: fix(ignore-rules): re-throw non-ENOENT errors from ignore file reads

question: When an ignore file cannot be read, should both shared scanners abort, skip only the affected subtree with a diagnostic, or continue scanning without those rules?
rationale: Ignore files control what the scanners consider, so continuing may inspect content that should have been excluded, while an uncaught throw can break existing discovery workflows; repository intent is needed before selecting the permanent boundary.

options.title: Skip subtree with diagnostic
options.body: Treat the affected subtree as unavailable, report the path and filesystem error through the caller's diagnostic surface, and continue unrelated scans.

options.title: Fail the complete scan
options.body: Intentionally fail closed for any non-ENOENT ignore-file error, with contextual errors, upgrade notes, focused tests, and real caller proof.

options.title: Keep best-effort behavior
options.body: Continue scanning despite ignore-file read failures, but emit a visible warning and document the risk of missing exclusion rules.

recommendation.title: Skip subtree with diagnostic
recommendation.body: Treat the affected subtree as unavailable, report the path and filesystem error through the caller's diagnostic surface, and continue unrelated scans.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the clearest recent history across both affected scanner implementations, though permanent ownership remains somewhat ambiguous.
